- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +10%+ from prior 3–5 days) with negative sentiment, cap forecast at 1–2 days above true outcome to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome is significantly below model (e.g., >10% gap) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, assume mean reversion — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, especially with low sentiment, reduce forecast by 3–7% per day to align with observed downward bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often overestimates near-term volatility — reduce forecast by 1–3% for days 1–7, then adjust to match true trend after day 8.
